apps.limitation: Enhancement can make existing edges and texture easier to see, but it cannot recover detail the camera never captured. Inspect faces, text, and fine patterns at full size before keeping the export.
apps.name: Unblurry
apps.value_prop: Blurry photo? Make it crystal clear.

apps.limitation: A phone scan is a convenient working copy, not automatically a certified original. Review every crop and OCR result, and follow the recipient's rules for signatures, identity, and retention.
apps.name: ScanTo Pro
apps.value_prop: Scan, organize, search, and protect documents on the device.

apps.limitation: Cycle estimates are informational patterns, not diagnosis, contraception, or a promise about fertility. Record what actually happens and consult a qualified clinician about concerning changes.
apps.name: Cyca
apps.value_prop: A warm, private way to understand your cycle.

assets.screen_description: trip spending summary and category view

apps.limitation: G+Money is a manual travel ledger, not a bank feed or accounting system. Exchange-rate totals are planning aids; verify card fees, cash conversions, receipts, and official reimbursement rules.
apps.name: G+Money
apps.value_prop: Convert and log travel spending in one place, including offline.

assets.screen_description: parent sound, music, and language settings

apps.limitation: The activities support practice but do not guarantee a reading milestone or replace an educator's assessment. An adult should choose a short session, observe comfort, and stop before frustration.
apps.name: Lumi Letters
apps.value_prop: Playful phonics, tracing, and letter practice for young learners.

apps.limitation: Aim990 supports study planning and practice; it does not guarantee a score or represent ETS. TOEIC is a trademark of ETS, which does not sponsor or endorse this page or app.
apps.name: Aim990
apps.value_prop: Daily listening and reading plans, weak-spot drills, and progress tracking.

apps.limitation: Sereno is an ambient-sound tool, not treatment for insomnia, tinnitus, anxiety, or another condition. Keep volume comfortable, preserve awareness when safety matters, and seek professional care for persistent symptoms.
apps.name: Sereno
apps.value_prop: Layer living sounds for sleep, focus, and calm, including offline.

units.image_context: checking a soft portrait before export
units.problem: A favorite portrait looks soft around the eyes, but aggressive sharpening could make skin and hair look artificial.
units.result: You get a reviewed portrait candidate, not an automatic promise that every blurred facial detail has been restored.
steps: Open the original portrait rather than a social-media copy.
Run one conservative enhancement and use the comparison control around eyes, hair, and edges.
Keep the export only if facial detail looks natural at full size.
units.title: How can I check a slightly soft portrait before sharing it?

units.image_context: reviewing mild motion softness in a pet photo
units.problem: The pet moved as the shutter fired, leaving usable color and shape but soft fur and eyes.
units.result: The useful outcome is a cleaner keepsake when source detail exists, while the untouched original remains available.
steps: Choose the least-compressed original in Photos.
Apply one enhancement pass and wait for the on-device preview.
Compare fur, whiskers, and eye boundaries before saving a separate copy.
units.title: Can I improve a pet photo with mild motion softness?

units.problem: A small scan has compression and soft edges, and the goal is a cleaner viewing copy without rewriting faces.
units.result: You finish with a cautiously reviewed derivative suitable for viewing, while preserving the archival scan.
steps: Duplicate the highest-resolution scan.
Try the mode that best matches the amount of softness, then inspect the preview.
Compare eyes, jewelry, fabric, and printed text before exporting.
units.title: How should I test enhancement on an old family-photo scan?

units.problem: Small paper receipts are easy to lose and thermal print can fade before an expense review.
units.result: You create a readable working archive tied to the trip while keeping any originals required for reimbursement.
steps: Place each receipt flat in even light and scan the full edges.
Name or categorize it while the purchase is still recognizable.
Open the resulting page and verify merchant, date, and total before filing.
units.title: How can I scan travel receipts before they fade?

units.problem: A mixed pile of receipts becomes difficult to review when files have generic names and no grouping.
units.result: You get a navigable receipt set for later review, not a substitute for tax or record-retention advice.
steps: Scan one receipt per clear page or logical multipage document.
Group and label scans by year and expense purpose.
Open a sample from every group and verify the important amounts are legible.
units.title: How do I organize a batch of tax receipts on iPhone?

units.problem: A long lease needs clean page edges and readable clauses, but the signed paper may still be the authoritative original.
units.result: The result is a readable reference copy with page order checked.
steps: Scan pages in order on a flat, evenly lit surface.
Review crop, contrast, and page sequence in the document viewer.
Export a working PDF and retain the signed original as required.
units.title: How can I make a readable working copy of a lease?

units.image_context: searching OCR text in lecture notes
units.problem: Printed handouts are hard to search when revising for a specific term or definition.
units.result: You gain a searchable study copy while the original page remains the authority.
steps: Scan pages flat and in order.
Run on-device OCR, then search for a known heading as a quality check.
Correct or annotate any OCR mistakes before relying on quoted text.
units.title: How can I turn printed lecture notes into searchable study material?

units.problem: A reference copy can be useful during travel, but identity information needs stronger local protection.
units.result: You retain a protected reference copy without treating it as a replacement for the original document.
steps: Confirm that making a copy is permitted for your use.
Scan every required edge and verify names and numbers.
Lock the document behind Face ID and keep the physical original secure.
units.title: How can I keep a private reference scan of a travel document?

units.image_context: sharing a signed form with a password
units.problem: A signed form may contain personal details and should not be sent as an unprotected, unchecked file.
units.result: You produce a reviewed, password-protected working copy while respecting the recipient's submission rules.
steps: Scan the complete form and verify signatures and dates.
Create the PDF and set a password when the recipient supports it.
Send the password through a separate agreed channel and keep the original.
units.title: How should I share a scanned signed form more carefully?

units.problem: A handout with charts and references becomes confusing if pages are cropped inconsistently or reordered.
units.result: You get a page-ordered working PDF whose visual quality has been checked.
steps: Capture every page with the same orientation.
Review the sharp multipage preview from first page to references.
Re-scan any unreadable chart label before exporting one PDF.
units.title: How do I scan a multipage research handout without losing page order?

units.problem: Some personal documents need to remain available without creating an unnecessary cloud copy.
units.result: You maintain a smaller local working archive with deliberate privacy and retention choices.
steps: Scan only the documents you genuinely need.
Review on-device processing and lock settings before filing.
Periodically remove expired records according to your own retention obligations.
units.title: How do I keep a small document archive on the device?

units.problem: Copying text from a scan saves typing, but OCR can silently change punctuation, names, or numbers.
units.result: You obtain editable text with a mandatory source-image verification step.
steps: Use settings appropriate to the page language and layout.
Run OCR and copy only the needed passage.
Compare every character of the quote with the page image before using it.
units.title: How can I extract a short quote from a scanned document responsibly?

units.problem: A single day can feel different from the last, and a concise context view may help with personal notes.
units.result: You get a private daily context plus a clearer separation between observation and prediction.
steps: Open today's overview and read the phase as an estimate.
Record what you actually observe rather than forcing it to match the forecast.
Escalate unusual or concerning symptoms to a qualified clinician.
units.title: How can I see today's cycle context without treating it as a diagnosis?

units.image_context: preparing a travel week with a body forecast
units.problem: Travel packing and breaks can be easier with advance context, but predicted timing may shift.
units.result: You prepare for plausible needs while keeping the travel plan flexible.
steps: Review the forecast as a range, not a guarantee.
Pack practical supplies and build flexible breaks into the itinerary.
Update the record with what actually happens during the trip.
units.title: How should I use a cycle forecast when preparing a travel week?

units.problem: Remembering dates from several weeks ago is unreliable when looking for a recurring personal pattern.
units.result: The calendar becomes an organized observation record rather than medical proof.
steps: Open the calendar and review recorded dates across more than one cycle.
Note changes in timing without labelling them normal or abnormal yourself.
Bring the record, not a self-diagnosis, to a clinician if you are concerned.
units.title: How do I review a cycle calendar for a personal pattern?

units.image_context: comparing energy notes with personal rhythm
units.problem: Energy changes are easy to remember selectively, so an on-device timeline can make the review more concrete.
units.result: You obtain a repeatable self-observation that can guide planning without overstating causality.
steps: Record energy in simple, consistent language.
Review the rhythm insight only after several entries exist.
Treat any apparent relationship as a personal observation, not a medical conclusion.
units.title: How can I compare my energy notes with cycle timing?

units.problem: A demanding routine can feel mismatched when energy is low, yet app suggestions cannot assess health or safety.
units.result: You make one reversible comfort adjustment without turning a suggestion into treatment.
steps: Check your actual condition before reading any suggestion.
Choose one low-stakes adjustment such as rest, hydration, or a shorter task.
Stop and seek advice if symptoms are severe or unusual.
units.title: How can I choose a gentler routine on a low-energy day?

units.image_context: planning a busy day with the smart planner
units.problem: A fixed schedule may be unrealistic on a low-energy day, but a cycle estimate should not dictate the day either.
units.result: You create a modest, adjustable plan based on current capacity.
steps: Check today's context and your actual energy.
Move one flexible task or break in the planner if needed.
Keep fixed commitments visible and reassess rather than assuming the forecast is certain.
units.title: How can I plan a busy day around how I actually feel?

units.problem: Small cash expenses disappear from memory quickly and never arrive through a bank feed.
units.result: The purchase is visible in the trip total instead of becoming an unexplained gap.
steps: Enter the amount in the currency you paid.
Choose the relevant trip and category while the receipt is in hand.
Check the home-currency estimate and retain the receipt if needed.
units.title: How can I log a small cash purchase abroad before I forget it?

units.image_context: reviewing a card purchase in the trip summary
units.problem: A card terminal amount is known immediately, but the issuer's final home-currency charge and fees may arrive later.
units.result: You preserve the transaction context while clearly separating an estimate from the bank's final amount.
steps: Log the local amount and category at purchase time.
Use the displayed conversion as a planning estimate.
Reconcile it against the settled card charge and fee later.
units.title: How should I record a card purchase with a pending final conversion?

units.problem: The app's reference conversion may not match the rate and commission actually paid at an exchange desk.
units.result: The ledger remains useful without pretending a reference rate equals your real cash rate.
steps: Record the real cash obtained and total home-currency cost separately.
Log purchases in the local currency as they occur.
Use your actual exchange receipt when calculating final travel cost.
units.title: How can I record spending after exchanging cash?

units.problem: Long sessions can turn a playful activity into resistance for a young learner.
units.result: The routine stays brief, predictable, and easier to repeat another day.
steps: Let the child choose one activity from the home screen.
Practice one letter or one short challenge.
Stop while engagement is still positive and note what to revisit.
units.title: How can we make a five-minute letter-practice routine?

units.problem: A young learner may benefit more from one focused sound than from moving quickly through the whole alphabet.
units.result: The session has one clear sound-letter goal and a natural stopping point.
steps: Choose one familiar letter.
Listen to the sound and connect it with the pictured word.
End after a successful repeat or recognition attempt.
units.title: How can a child practice one letter sound without a long lesson?

units.problem: A child may know a capital letter but not recognize the lowercase shape in books.
units.result: The child practices visual equivalence without turning the session into a test.
steps: Pick one uppercase and lowercase pair from the letter grid.
Say the shared sound while pointing to both forms.
Find the same pair once more, then stop or switch activities.
units.title: How can we compare uppercase and lowercase forms?

units.problem: A progress screen can guide the next activity, but percentages do not define a child's ability or readiness.
units.result: Progress becomes a planning clue, not a label or promise about learning.
steps: Review which activities were attempted and which were repeated.
Choose one comfortable next step rather than chasing completion.
Observe the child directly and adjust pace when the screen and behavior differ.
units.title: How can a parent use progress without turning it into a grade?

units.problem: Repeated tracing is less useful when the child rushes or loses the intended stroke path.
units.result: The activity becomes a short stroke-order practice rather than a volume target.
steps: Choose one uppercase letter and watch the starting point.
Trace slowly along the guide with a comfortable finger movement.
Repeat only while the child remains relaxed and interested.
units.title: How can a child trace one uppercase letter carefully?

units.image_context: ending practice at the letter-galaxy reward screen
units.problem: A reward screen can become a cue to continue indefinitely unless the stopping point is clear.
units.result: The reward supports a positive ending instead of extending screen time automatically.
steps: Agree on one final activity before starting.
Acknowledge the earned in-app progress or reward.
Close the session and name what the child enjoyed rather than demanding another level.
units.title: How can we use an in-app reward to end a session well?

units.problem: A child may benefit from feeling pencil movement after learning the shape on screen.
units.result: The same letter is practiced in a screen-free format without requiring a long worksheet session.
steps: Choose a worksheet for one familiar letter.
Print it and set up a comfortable pencil grip and surface.
Do a small number of traces, then keep or recycle the sheet based on the child's interest.
units.title: How can we move one letter from screen practice to paper?

units.problem: A child may recognize a letter in isolation but hesitate when several shapes appear together.
units.result: The game practices discrimination with feedback rather than memorized guessing.
steps: Name the target letter before choices appear.
Let the child compare curves and lines and choose the matching shape.
If the choice is wrong, describe one visual clue and try once more.
units.title: How can a matching game reinforce letter shape?

units.image_context: finding the letter that matches a sound
units.problem: Listening and visual recognition need to connect without adding too many choices at once.
units.result: The child links one heard sound with one written form in a contained activity.
steps: Play one letter sound.
Ask the child to find the matching letter among the visible options.
Replay the sound and say it together before moving on.
units.title: How can we practice hearing and finding a letter sound?

units.problem: Music or effects can help engagement for one child and distract another.
units.result: The audio environment is intentionally adjusted to the child and setting.
steps: Open parent settings before handing over the device.
Set music and effects to a comfortable level for the room.
Observe one activity and revise the balance if speech or focus is harder.
units.title: How can a parent set comfortable sound for letter practice?

units.problem: A target score is not a plan unless available days and listening or reading needs become specific sessions.
units.result: You get a concrete sequence of practice days without a guarantee that the target score will be reached.
steps: Complete the diagnostic or baseline review honestly.
Use the daily plan to identify one listening and one reading priority.
Record completion and revise the next week from actual performance.
units.title: How can I turn a 30-day TOEIC study target into daily work?

units.problem: Untimed accuracy alone does not reveal where pacing breaks down.
units.result: You obtain a bounded pacing sample that can guide the next practice block.
steps: Choose one listening or reading part rather than a full exam.
Use the available timer and answer without pausing to research.
Review both errors and where time was spent before repeating.
units.title: How can I practice one TOEIC part under time pressure?

units.problem: A total practice score hides whether errors come from pace, vocabulary, detail, or a specific question format.
units.result: You convert one weakness label into a specific practice-and-review loop.
steps: Open the weak-skill view and choose one listening category.
Complete a focused drill under realistic audio conditions.
Review why each missed answer was tempting before selecting the next drill.
units.title: How can I act on a weak listening category?

units.problem: A full mock can be too costly when the goal is a quick pacing check or the available time is short.
units.result: You get a compact performance snapshot with an immediate review step.
steps: Choose the mini mock that fits the available block.
Complete it under uninterrupted test-like conditions.
Review the result by skill and schedule follow-up practice instead of extrapolating a guaranteed score.
units.title: When is a mini mock test more useful than a full mock?

units.image_context: choosing a gentle sound for a quiet room
units.problem: A very quiet room can make small household noises feel more noticeable, but louder sound is not automatically better.
units.result: You create a modest, reversible ambient layer without claiming a sleep treatment.
steps: Choose one neutral sound from the library.
Start at a low, comfortable volume.
Listen for several minutes and lower or stop it if it masks important sounds or feels tiring.
units.title: How can I add gentle background sound to a room that feels too quiet?

units.problem: A repeatable cue can support a routine, but sound alone does not diagnose or cure sleep difficulty.
units.result: You establish a consistent environmental cue without making a medical promise.
steps: Choose one calm scene before getting into bed.
Set a low volume and pair it with the same wind-down steps.
Stop using it if it becomes irritating or interferes with hearing what matters.
units.title: How can I use one ambient scene as a bedtime cue?

units.image_context: mixing sound around intermittent apartment noise
units.problem: Uneven outside noise can be distracting, but an overly dense mix may become another source of fatigue.
units.result: The room gains a consistent background layer while awareness and comfort remain priorities.
steps: Choose one steady base sound.
Add only one complementary layer and balance both at a comfortable volume.
Keep alarms and safety-relevant sounds audible and revise the mix as conditions change.
units.title: How can I build an ambient mix for an intermittently noisy apartment?

hypothesis: Internal discovery plus a regular sitemap improves crawl, index, Google Images impressions, and clicks versus image-sitemap-only discovery across preregistered unique image-page units.

design.asset_ownership: one image URL belongs to one page and one arm
design.assignment: preregistered SHA-256 ranked complete randomization within App strata
design.treatment: linked hub + regular sitemap + image sitemap
design.holdout: image sitemap only; no internal inbound link
design.analysis: stratified randomization inference with App-stratum differences weighted by stratum size
design.pairing_claim: none; heterogeneous authentic screenshots are randomized units, not same-image or pure-page matched pairs
design.technical_parity: Both arms have a standard img, natural alt/caption, max-image-preview:large, ImageObject, SoftwareApplication, and the same App×Google Images Apple campaign policy. Creative heterogeneity is handled by stratification and randomization inference.

interpretation.market_result_requires: indexed URL and at least 42 completed days after activation
interpretation.maximum_window: freeze the primary read at 56 days; later data is follow-up
